answer: Each agent must post a bond from a scarce, slashable vault before its votes count; the protocol lets any participant challenge duplicate identities by presenting signed messages that link them to the same controlling key or reused credentials. If the challenge succeeds, the linked agents lose their bonds and their votes are removed. A quill-signed audit record at each vertex makes evidence checkable, so an attacker must lock up real capital for every identity and risks losing it when sybils are exposed.
